claim: Neonatal brachial plexus injury (NBPI) occurs in approximately 1.5 of every 1000 live births.
source: Injury to the brachial plexus at birth (neonatal brachial plexus injury – NBPI) is the most common cause of upper limb paralysis in children (Foad et al., 2008), occurring in approximately 1.5 of every 1000 live births, in both females and males at an equal rate (McLaren et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McLaren et al., 2019.

claim: NBPI occurs in both females and males at an equal rate.
source: Injury to the brachial plexus at birth (neonatal brachial plexus injury – NBPI) is the most common cause of upper limb paralysis in children (Foad et al., 2008), occurring in approximately 1.5 of every 1000 live births, in both females and males at an equal rate (McLaren et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McLaren et al., 2019.

claim: NBPI leads to permanent neurologic deficits in 20–40% of affected children.
source: This initial nerve injury leads to permanent neurologic deficits in 20–40% of affected children (Govindan and Burrows, 2019; Pondaag et al., 2004), and results in the secondary formation of disabling and incurable muscle contractures, or joint stiffness.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Govindan and Burrows, 2019 and Pondaag et al., 2004.

claim: Contractures result from impaired longitudinal muscle growth characterized by overstretch/elongation of sarcomeres in denervated muscles.
source: Using a mouse model of NBPI, we previously discovered that contractures result from impaired longitudinal muscle growth, as characterized by the overstretch/elongation of sarcomeres in denervated muscles (Nikolaou et al., 2011; Weekley et al., 2012; Nikolaou et al., 2014; Nikolaou et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple prior studies by the authors.

claim: Deficits in muscle length after NBPI are independent of satellite cell-mediated myonuclear accretion.
source: Such deficits in muscle length are independent of satellite cell-mediated myonuclear accretion, but are instead caused by aberrant levels of muscle protein degradation associated with increased catalytic activity of the 20S proteasome (Nikolaou et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nikolaou et al., 2019.

claim: Deficits in muscle length after NBPI are caused by aberrant levels of muscle protein degradation associated with increased catalytic activity of the 20S proteasome.
source: Such deficits in muscle length are independent of satellite cell-mediated myonuclear accretion, but are instead caused by aberrant levels of muscle protein degradation associated with increased catalytic activity of the 20S proteasome (Nikolaou et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nikolaou et al., 2019.

claim: Inhibition of the proteasome with bortezomib restores sarcomere length and reduces contracture formation.
source: As proof of concept, we showed that inhibition of the proteasome with an FDA-approved proteasome inhibitor, bortezomib, restores sarcomere length and reduces contracture formation (Nikolaou et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nikolaou et al., 2019.

claim: Bortezomib treatment is required throughout postnatal development to prevent contractures at skeletal maturity.
source: We recently reported that bortezomib treatment is required throughout postnatal development to prevent contractures at skeletal maturity, and that its efficacy is diminished beyond the neonatal period (Goh et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Goh et al., 2021.

claim: The efficacy of bortezomib is diminished beyond the neonatal period.
source: We recently reported that bortezomib treatment is required throughout postnatal development to prevent contractures at skeletal maturity, and that its efficacy is diminished beyond the neonatal period (Goh et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Goh et al., 2021.

claim: MSTN is a myokine and a member of the transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) superfamily.
source: MSTN, also known as growth differentiation factor-8 (GDF8), is a myokine and a member of the transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) superfamily (Lee, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lee, 2004.

claim: Ligand binding of MSTN to its Type 2 receptors activates the downstream Smad proteins 2 and 3.
source: In normally innervated skeletal muscles, ligand binding of MSTN to its Type 2 receptors, ACVR2 (ActRIIA) and ACVR2B (ActRIIB), activates the downstream Smad proteins 2 and 3 (Sartori et al., 2009; Trendelenburg et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sartori et al., 2009 and Trendelenburg et al., 2009.

claim: MSTN signaling regulates muscle homeostasis by increasing degradation and decreasing Akt/mTOR-mediated synthesis.
source: These signaling events regulate muscle homeostasis by increasing degradation and decreasing Akt/mTOR-mediated synthesis, ultimately attenuating muscle size and limiting aberrant growth (Lee, 2004; Lee, 2012; Lee, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lee, 2004, Lee, 2012, and Lee, 2021.

claim: MSTN functions as a negative regulator of muscle mass and protein balance.
source: MSTN thereby functions as a negative regulator of muscle mass and protein balance.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the preceding discussion of MSTN's role in regulating muscle homeostasis.

claim: Pharmacologic inhibition of MSTN signaling induces hypertrophy in normally innervated muscles of both female and male mice.
source: Our findings revealed that inhibition of the MSTN pathway resulted in robust growth of normally innervated forelimb muscles in both neonatal female and male mice. Specifically, MSTN inhibition enhanced cross-sectional and volumetric growth of the brachialis muscles (Figure 1B–D), as well as increased overall muscle weight and elevated total protein levels in biceps muscles (Figure 1F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1 and described in the text.

claim: MSTN inhibition results in greater increases in brachialis volume, biceps weight, and biceps total protein content in females than males compared to respective controls.
source: Despite this, the increases in brachialis volume (61% vs. 35%), biceps weight (49% vs. 35%), and biceps total protein content (47% vs. 28%) were greater in females than males when compared to respective controls (Figure 1E, H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data presented in Figure 1E and H.

claim: ACVR2B-Fc treatment attenuates humerus length and heart size in male mice.
source: Curiously, ACVR2B-Fc treatment did not yield additional gains in body weight but instead attenuated humerus length and heart size in male mice, whereas female mice had smaller spleens after treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: ACVR2B-Fc treatment results in smaller spleens in female mice.
source: Curiously, ACVR2B-Fc treatment did not yield additional gains in body weight but instead attenuated humerus length and heart size in male mice, whereas female mice had smaller spleens after treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pharmacologic blockade of MSTN signaling reduces muscle loss of denervated brachialis and biceps muscles only in female mice.
source: In contrast to normally innervated neonatal muscles, pharmacologic blockade of MSTN signaling reduced muscle loss of denervated brachialis and biceps muscles only in female mice (Figure 2A–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2.

claim: MSTN inhibition increases brachialis cross-sectional area and volume by 25–26% in denervated female muscles.
source: In denervated female muscles, MSTN inhibition specifically increased brachialis cross-sectional area and volume by 25–26%, and biceps weight and total protein by 31–50%.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from the study.

claim: MSTN inhibition increases biceps weight and total protein by 31–50% in denervated female muscles.
source: In denervated female muscles, MSTN inhibition specifically increased brachialis cross-sectional area and volume by 25–26%, and biceps weight and total protein by 31–50%.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data from the study.

claim: ACVR2B-Fc treatment fails to increase brachialis muscle CSA and volume in denervated male muscles.
source: However, there were no improvements with MSTN inhibition in denervated male muscles, as ACVR2B-Fc treatment failed to increase brachialis muscle CSA and volume (Figure 2A–C), or biceps muscle weight and total protein levels (Figure 2D, E) in male mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2.

claim: ACVR2B-Fc treatment improved passive range of motion in both elbow and shoulder joints only in female mice 4 weeks post-NBPI.
source: Indeed, we discovered that ACVR2B-Fc treatment improved passive range of motion in both elbow and shoulder joints only in female mice 4 weeks post-NBPI (Figure 3A, B, D, E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3.

claim: ACVR2B-Fc treatment reduces both elbow flexion and shoulder rotation contracture severity in female, but not male mice.
source: This sex-specific improvement in joint mobility corresponded to a reduction in both elbow flexion and shoulder rotation contracture severity in female, but not male mice (Figure 3C, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Neonatal MSTN inhibition rescues sarcomere length in the denervated brachialis muscles of female mice.
source: Here, we observed that neonatal MSTN inhibition rescued sarcomere length (reduced sarcomere elongation) in the denervated brachialis muscles of female mice (Figure 4A–C), indicating an improvement in functional muscle length (Goh et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Sarcomeres in the denervated brachialis of male mice remain overstretched after MSTN inhibition.
source: Conversely, sarcomeres in the denervated brachialis of male mice remained overstretched, an indication of impaired longitudinal muscle growth.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations described in the text.

claim: Contracture formation following neonatal muscle denervation in female mice is driven by MSTN-dependent impairment of longitudinal muscle growth.
source: Hence, our collective findings establish that contracture formation following neonatal muscle denervation in female mice is driven by MSTN-dependent impairment of longitudinal muscle growth.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: 4 weeks of NBPI drives protein synthesis in denervated biceps muscles.
source: Through western blot analysis of puromycin incorporation (Goodman et al., 2011; Schmidt et al., 2009), we discovered that while 4 weeks of NBPI drove protein synthesis in denervated biceps muscles, MSTN inhibition does not augment this increase in either sex (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 5.

claim: MSTN inhibition does not augment the denervation-induced increase in protein synthesis in either sex.
source: Through western blot analysis of puromycin incorporation (Goodman et al., 2011; Schmidt et al., 2009), we discovered that while 4 weeks of NBPI drove protein synthesis in denervated biceps muscles, MSTN inhibition does not augment this increase in either sex (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Perturbations in Akt activity and total protein expression in denervated triceps muscles are not further impacted by ACVR2B-Fc treatment at 4 weeks post-NBPI.
source: This finding was corroborated by western blot analyses of the Akt/mTOR hypertrophic signaling pathway (Bodine et al., 2001; Rommel et al., 2001; Egerman and Glass, 2014; Sartori et al., 2021), which revealed that perturbations in Akt activity and total protein expression in denervated triceps muscles were not further impacted by ACVR2B-Fc treatment at 4 weeks post-NBPI (Figure 5C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 5.

claim: MSTN-mediated proteostasis dysregulation in denervated female muscles occurs independent of Akt/mTOR-mediated protein synthesis.
source: These collective findings therefore indicate that MSTN-mediated proteostasis dysregulation in denervated female muscles occurs independent of Akt/mTOR-mediated protein synthesis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental findings on protein synthesis and Akt/mTOR signaling.

claim: Denervation increases polyubiquitination of proteins greater than 40 kDa.
source: While total levels of K48-linked polyubiquitin were not different between normally innervated and denervated biceps muscles, we observed increased polyubiquitination of proteins greater than 40 kDa (Figure 6A–D), similar to what we have reported before (Nikolaou et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 6 and a citation to prior work.

claim: MSTN inhibition does not attenuate the denervation-induced increases in proteins tagged for degradation at the >40 kDa molecular weight range in either sex.
source: However, MSTN inhibition did not attenuate the denervation-induced increases in proteins tagged for degradation at this molecular weight range in either sex.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations described in the text.

claim: MSTN inhibition does not alter protein levels of the muscle-specific E3 ligases, MuRF1 and Atrogin-1.
source: Further investigation revealed that MSTN inhibition did not alter protein levels of the muscle-specific E3 ligases, MuRF1 and Atrogin-1, (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Denervation decreased MuRF1 at 4 weeks post-NBPI.
source: Unexpectedly, denervation decreased MuRF1 and did not change Atrogin-1 levels at 4 weeks post-NBPI, which differ from our earlier reports of increased transcriptional activity of MuRF1 at 2 weeks post-NBPI (Nikolaou et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and comparison to prior work.

claim: Denervation did not change Atrogin-1 levels at 4 weeks post-NBPI.
source: Unexpectedly, denervation decreased MuRF1 and did not change Atrogin-1 levels at 4 weeks post-NBPI, which differ from our earlier reports of increased transcriptional activity of MuRF1 at 2 weeks post-NBPI (Nikolaou et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: ACVR2B-Fc effectively reduces the catalytic activity of the 20S proteasome β5 subunit in denervated triceps muscles only in female mice.
source: Instead, ACVR2B-Fc effectively reduced the catalytic activity of the 20S proteasome β5 subunit in denervated triceps muscles only in female mice (Figure 6E, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 6.

claim: MSTN regulates sex-specific proteostasis dysregulation by circumventing polyubiquitination and directly targeting the proteasome.
source: As K48-linked ubiquitin chains are the most prevalent signal that mark protein substrates for proteasome degradation (Yau and Rape, 2016), these findings suggest that MSTN regulates sex-specific proteostasis dysregulation by circumventing polyubiquitination and directly targeting the proteasome.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental findings on ubiquitination and proteasome activity, along with knowledge about K48-linked ubiquitin chains.

claim: Neonatal denervation increases both Smad2 and Smad3 phosphorylation and translation in a sex-independent manner.
source: Here, we observed sex-independent increases in both Smad2 and Smad3 phosphorylation and translation with neonatal denervation, which were not further altered with MSTN inhibition (Figure 7A–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 7.

claim: MSTN inhibition does not alter Smad2/3 phosphorylation and translation after neonatal denervation.
source: Here, we observed sex-independent increases in both Smad2 and Smad3 phosphorylation and translation with neonatal denervation, which were not further altered with MSTN inhibition (Figure 7A–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 7.

claim: MSTN plays a sex-specific role in muscle proteostasis dysregulation after neonatal denervation through non-canonical signaling pathways.
source: Our collective findings thus posit a sex-specific role for MSTN in muscle proteostasis dysregulation after neonatal denervation through non-canonical signaling pathways.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental findings showing effects on proteasome activity without changes in canonical pathways.

claim: Bortezomib treatment preferentially prevents elbow and shoulder contractures in male mice throughout postnatal development and into skeletal maturity.
source: In contrast with MSTN inhibition, we observed greater and more consistent reductions in elbow and shoulder contracture severity across the different time points in male mice with bortezomib treatment (Figure 8B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by reanalysis of prior data presented in Figure 8.

claim: Bortezomib improves longitudinal muscle growth in female and male mice, except at 8 weeks of treatment.
source: Sex differences in sarcomere length were less apparent, as bortezomib improved longitudinal muscle growth in female and male mice, except at 8 w of treatment (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is supported by reanalysis of prior data presented in Figure 8.

claim: Bortezomib attenuates β1 subunit activity at 8 and 12 weeks only in male mice.
source: Lastly, while bortezomib did not alter β5 subunit activity in either sex (Figure 8E, F), it attenuated β1 subunit activity at 8 and 12 w only in male mice (Figure 8G, H).
evidence: The claim is supported by reanalysis of prior data presented in Figure 8.

claim: A 30–45% attenuation in either β1 or β5 subunit activity at 4 weeks post-NBPI is associated with a 50–55% and a 45–60% reduction in elbow and shoulder contractures, respectively.
source: Intriguingly, the effects of MSTN inhibition on proteasome activity in female mice parallel our earlier results of proteasome inhibition with bortezomib (Goh et al., 2021). Specifically, we observed that a 30–45% attenuation in either β1 or β5 subunit activity at 4 weeks post-NBPI is associated with a 50–55% and a 45–60% reduction in elbow and shoulder contractures, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of data from the current and prior studies.

claim: A 30–45% attenuation in either β1 or β5 subunit activity is associated with an improvement of normalized sarcomere length by 14–15%.
source: Furthermore, this magnitude of reduction in either subunit activity is associated with an improvement of normalized sarcomere length by 14–15%.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of data from the study.

claim: Different upstream pathways in contracture formation between sexes ultimately converge at the 20S proteasome.
source: Nevertheless, our collective findings indicate that different upstream pathways in contracture formation between sexes ultimately converge at the 20S proteasome, thereby validating the role of the proteasome as a key mediator of NBPI-induced contractures.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective findings on sex-specific effects of MSTN and bortezomib on proteasome activity.

claim: Pharmacologic inhibition of MSTN signaling with ACVR2B-Fc has been shown to induce robust muscle growth in adult mice.
source: While pharmacologic inhibition of MSTN signaling with the soluble ACVR2B-Fc decoy receptor has been shown to induce robust muscle growth in adult mice (Lee et al., 2005), it has not been validated in neonatal mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2005.

claim: Pharmacologic MSTN inhibition with ACVR2B-Fc has not been validated in neonatal mice prior to this study.
source: While pharmacologic inhibition of MSTN signaling with the soluble ACVR2B-Fc decoy receptor has been shown to induce robust muscle growth in adult mice (Lee et al., 2005), it has not been validated in neonatal mice.
evidence: The claim is stated explicitly in the text.

claim: Pharmacologic MSTN inhibition enhances skeletal muscle growth at P33, which is equivalent to the completion of neonatal muscle development in human infants.
source: First, we discovered that pharmacologic MSTN inhibition with ACVR2B-Fc enhanced the size and protein content of normally innervated forelimb muscles in 1-month-old mice at P33, which is equivalent to the completion of neonatal muscle development in human infants (Dutta and Sengupta, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental findings and a citation to Dutta and Sengupta, 2016.

claim: The youngest age that prior studies on MSTN inhibition have reported gains in lean body mass was in 2-month-old mice.
source: In comparison, the youngest age that prior studies on MSTN inhibition have reported gains in lean body mass was in 2-month-old mice (McPherron and Lee, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McPherron and Lee, 2002.

claim: Female and male muscles typically display heterogeneity in body composition and protein turnover.
source: Female and male muscles typically display heterogeneity in body composition and protein turnover (Griffin and Goldspink, 1973; Smith and Mittendorfer, 2016), regenerative and hypertrophic processes (Kitajima and Ono, 2016; Seko et al., 2020), metabolism and substrate utilization (Rosa-Caldwell and Greene, 2019; Maher et al., 2009), drug pharmacodynamics (Salamone et al., 2022), and even the development of disease-induced pathologies (De Jonghe et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: Ubiquitin-independent proteasomal degradation has been supported by several prior studies in a subset of proteins belonging to the Intrinsic Disordered Protein (IDP) family.
source: Indeed, the phenomenon of ubiquitin-independent proteasomal degradation has been supported by several prior studies in a subset of proteins, which share common features of belonging to the Intrinsic Disordered Protein (IDP) family (Erales and Coffino, 2014; Jariel-Encontre et al., 2008), such as p21 and p53 (Asher et al., 2005; Chen et al., 2004; Tsvetkov et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: Targeted deletion of MSTN during skeletal maturity increased masseter mass and bite force in male mice only.
source: Targeted deletion of MSTN during skeletal maturity increased masseter mass and bite force in male mice only (Williams et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Williams et al., 2015.

claim: Long-term MSTN deletion in skeletal muscles increased lean muscle mass only in aged female mice.
source: In contrast, long-term MSTN deletion in skeletal muscles increased lean muscle mass only in aged female mice (Tavoian et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tavoian et al., 2019.

claim: Women tend to have higher gene expression of the ACVR2B receptor compared to men.
source: Indeed, while men are prone to having higher expression of genes encoding ribosomal and mitochondrial proteins, women tend to have higher gene expression of the ACVR2B receptor (Welle et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Welle et al., 2008.

claim: There is increased transcriptional and translational expression of latent MSTN in hindlimb muscles of adult female mice compared to their male counterparts.
source: Moreover, there is an increased transcriptional and translational expression of latent MSTN in hindlimb muscles of adult female mice compared to their male counterparts (McMahon et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McMahon et al., 2003.

claim: In a juvenile mouse model of sciatic nerve resection, ACVR2B-Fc treatment was unable to prevent atrophy in male mice.
source: In a juvenile mouse model of sciatic nerve resection, MacDonald et al. reported an inability of both rapamycin and ACVR2B-Fc treatment to prevent atrophy in male mice, and surmised that denervation atrophy is not Akt/mTOR or MSTN-dependent (MacDonald et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to MacDonald et al., 2014.

claim: Sex differences in the pathophysiology of muscle atrophy have been documented in an adult mouse model of tenotomy.
source: Importantly, the sex dimorphisms in muscle atrophy are not limited to neonatal denervation, as sex differences in the pathophysiology of muscle atrophy have also been documented by an independent group using an adult mouse model of tenotomy (Meyer et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Meyer et al., 2022.

claim: The broad ligand specificity of ACVR2B-Fc increases the risk of toxicity to non-skeletal muscle tissues and cell types.
source: Indeed, the broad ligand specificity of ACVR2B-Fc increases the risk of toxicity to non-skeletal muscle tissues and cell types, ranging from epistaxis to telangiectasias (Campbell et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Campbell et al., 2017.

claim: MSTN plays a key role in cardiac energy homeostasis.
source: As MSTN plays a key role in cardiac energy homeostasis (Biesemann et al., 2014), the attenuation in heart size of male mice could impair cardiac function and lead to reduced muscle activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Biesemann et al., 2014.

claim: Prior studies have failed to find an effect of embryonic MSTN deletion on humerus length in adult mice.
source: Prior studies have failed to find an effect of embryonic MSTN deletion on humerus length in adult mice, although the use of a mixed-sex approach may have masked sex-related differences (Hamrick et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hamrick et al., 2002.

claim: p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1) signaling has recently been shown to be permissive to gains in skeletal muscle mass with MSTN inhibition.
source: Potential non-canonical pathways could include p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1) signaling, which has recently been shown to be permissive to gains in skeletal muscle mass with MSTN inhibition (Barbé et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Barbé et al., 2021.

claim: Many members of the TGF-β superfamily, such as Activin A and GDF-11, are capable of binding Activin Type IIB receptors.
source: Previous studies have reported that many members of the TGF-β superfamily, such as Activin A and GDF-11, are capable of binding Activin Type IIB receptors (Oh et al., 2002; Olsen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Oh et al., 2002 and Olsen et al., 2015.

claim: Simultaneous inhibition of MSTN and Activin A leads to more effective muscle hypertrophy and force production in rodents and primates.
source: Of note, simultaneous inhibition of MSTN and Activin A leads to more effective muscle hypertrophy and force production in rodents and primates (Latres et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Latres et al., 2017.

claim: A sex-specific role for Activin A in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)-induced cachexia has been reported.
source: Indeed, a sex-specific role for Activin A in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)-induced cachexia has recently been reported by Zhong et al., 2022.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhong et al., 2022.

claim: Sex-specific differences in endogenous levels of Activin A contribute to sex dimorphisms in PDAC-induced cachexia.
source: The authors observed that sex-specific differences in endogenous levels of Activin A contribute to sex dimorphisms in PDAC-induced cachexia, as well as the differential outcomes of ACVR2B-Fc treatment in attenuating tumor-induced Activin (Zhong et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhong et al., 2022.

claim: Contracture formation plateaus at 4 weeks post-NBPI.
source: Furthermore, we have previously established that contracture formation plateaus at 4 weeks post-NBPI, making this time point ideal for such a proof of concept investigation.
evidence: The claim is based on prior work by the authors.

claim: Unilateral, global (C5–T1), post-ganglionic NBPIs were surgically created in P5 wildtype female and male mice by extraforaminal nerve root excision.
source: Briefly, unilateral, global (C5–T1), post-ganglionic NBPIs were surgically created in P5 wildtype female and male mice (Charles River; CD-1 IGS mouse, strain code 022) by extraforaminal nerve root excision under isoflurane anesthesia.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: The soluble decoy receptor ACVR2B-Fc was administered weekly at a dose of 10 mg/kg via intraperitoneal injections.
source: Hence, the soluble decoy receptor was administered weekly at a dose of 10 mg/kg via intraperitoneal injections, whereas Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) was used as a control in a separate litter of mice (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: A total of 32 mice (17 female and 15 male) were used in this study.
source: A total of 32 mice (17 female – 10 control, 7 experimental; and 15 male – 8 control, 7 experimental) were used in this study.
evidence: The claim describes the sample size used in the study.
